title: Lab Basics
description: Three short lessons on working safely at the bench, then a quiz. About fifteen minutes.

blocks.text:
Most lab accidents start with something small: a missing pair of goggles, a flask set down too close to the edge, a spill left for later.

This course walks through the habits that prevent them. Each lesson takes a few minutes, and you can come back to any of them from the outline.
Everything on this bench has a job. Goggles and gloves protect you, the spill kit and eyewash station are there for when something goes wrong.

items: Choose protective equipment for the task in front of you
Respond to a spill calmly and in the right order
Check what you learned in a short quiz

blocks.text: Safety is a habit you practise before you need it.

blocks.label: Already confident? Go to the quiz
blocks.text: You can take the quiz at any time.
Protective equipment only works when it is the right kind and worn the right way. Open each item to see when it matters.

items.title: Safety goggles
items.text: Wear them whenever liquids are poured, heated or shaken, even for a quick task. Ordinary glasses do not seal at the sides.

items.title: Gloves
items.text: Match the glove material to the chemical. Change gloves as soon as they are torn or contaminated, and never touch door handles or phones with them.

items.title: Lab coat
items.text: Keep it buttoned and leave it in the lab, so whatever it caught does not travel home with you.

items.title: Before
items.text: Read the label and the safety sheet. Put on goggles, gloves and coat before you open anything.

items.title: During
items.text: Keep containers away from the bench edge and work with the smallest amount that does the job.

items.title: After
items.text: Close and label containers, wipe the bench, then take gloves off last and wash your hands.

blocks.prompt: You are about to heat a solution. Which item is essential?

choices.label: Safety goggles
choices.feedback: Right. Heated liquids can spit without warning.

choices.label: Sandals
choices.feedback: Open shoes are never safe at the bench.

choices.label: A scarf
choices.feedback: Loose clothing is a hazard near heat.

blocks.text: Next, you will put these habits to work on a spill.

blocks.intro: A beaker tips over and liquid spreads across the bench. Work through the response one step at a time.

items.title: Warn
items.text: Tell the people around you, clearly and at once.

items.title: Step back
items.text: Move out of splash range and keep others away.

items.title: Assess
items.text: Identify the liquid from its label. Unknown or large spills go straight to your supervisor.

items.title: Clean up
items.text: Use the spill kit, never paper towels, then report what happened.

blocks.summary: Warn, step back, assess, clean up. In that order, every time.

items.title: Goggles
items.text: Within reach, not in a drawer.

items.title: Flask
items.text: Set well back from the edge of the bench.

items.title: Spill kit
items.text: Absorbent pads and neutralisers for small spills.

items.title: Eyewash
items.text: Rinse for at least fifteen minutes if anything reaches your eyes.
Warn people nearby
Wipe it up with paper towels
Use the spill kit
Leave it for the next person

items.title: Spill happens
items.text: Stop what you are doing.

items.title: Warn and step back
items.text: Voice first, then distance.

items.title: Clean up
items.text: Spill kit, gloves, goggles.

items.title: Report
items.text: Write down what spilled and how.

items: I know where the spill kit is
I know where the eyewash station is
